title: Device Fingerprinting Security Checklist - Protect Your Privacy
metaDescription: Complete checklist to protect against device fingerprinting. Stop invisible tracking that persists after clearing cookies with these proven methods.
intro: Device fingerprinting allows websites to track you even after clearing cookies by collecting unique information about your browser and device. This checklist provides actionable steps to protect against these invisible tracking techniques.

items.why: WebGL fingerprinting analyzes your graphics card capabilities to create a unique identifier that's nearly impossible to change.
items.howTo: In Firefox: type about:config, search for webgl.disabled and set to true. In Chrome: use flags --disable-webgl or install uBlock Origin to block WebGL.

items.task: Block or spoof HTML5 Canvas fingerprinting
items.why: Canvas fingerprinting forces your browser to draw hidden images, creating unique signatures based on your system's rendering differences.
items.howTo: Install Canvas Blocker extension for Firefox or Use a privacy-focused browser which has built-in canvas protection. Enable 'Block canvas fingerprinting' in settings.

items.task: Disable WebRTC to prevent IP leaks
items.why: WebRTC can expose your real IP address even when using VPN and provides additional fingerprinting data points.
items.howTo: Firefox: Set media.peerconnection.enabled to false in about:config. Chrome: Install WebRTC Leak Prevent extension or Use a privacy-focused browser.

items.why: Unique User-Agent strings reveal specific browser versions, operating systems, and device information that contribute to your fingerprint.
items.howTo: Install User-Agent Switcher extension and select a common Windows Chrome user agent. Avoid rare or outdated user agents that stand out.

items.why: Installed plugins create unique fingerprint combinations. Flash, Java, and PDF plugins are commonly fingerprinted.
items.howTo: Go to browser settings, find plugins/extensions section, and disable Flash, Java, Silverlight, and other non-essential plugins. Keep only critical ones.

items.why: Your timezone is easily accessible to websites and combined with other data points creates a more unique fingerprint profile.
items.howTo: Use Timezone Guard extension to spoof your timezone to UTC, or Use a privacy-focused browser which includes timezone protection in privacy mode.

items.why: Audio fingerprinting analyzes how your system processes audio signals, creating unique identifiers based on hardware differences.
items.howTo: Install AudioContext Fingerprint Defender extension or use browsers with built-in audio protection like a privacy-focused browser or Tor Browser.

items.why: Websites can detect installed fonts on your system, creating unique combinations that identify your device across different sites.
items.howTo: Use uBlock Origin with filter lists that block font enumeration, or switch to a privacy-focused browser which limits font detection capabilities.

items.why: Unique screen resolutions, especially on mobile devices or multi-monitor setups, create easily identifiable fingerprint signatures.
items.howTo: Use Resolution Changer extension to report common resolutions like 1920x1080, or browse in full-screen mode to limit resolution detection.

items.why: CPU cores, memory, graphics cards, and other hardware specs create highly unique fingerprints that are difficult to change.
items.howTo: Use browsers that limit hardware API access like Tor Browser, or enable strict privacy settings in Firefox about:config for hardware queries.

items.why: Battery level and charging status provide additional unique identifiers, especially on mobile devices with varying battery health.
items.howTo: Firefox: Set dom.battery.enabled to false in about:config. Chrome: Install extensions that block battery API or use privacy-focused browsers.

items.why: Regular testing helps you understand how unique your browser appears and whether your protection measures are working effectively.
items.howTo: Visit AmIUnique.org, Panopticlick.eff.org, and BrowserLeaks.com monthly to test your fingerprint. Document changes after implementing protections.

items.task: Use different browsers for different activities
items.why: Compartmentalizing your browsing creates separate fingerprint profiles, making it harder to track your activities across different contexts.
items.howTo: Use a privacy-focused browser or Tor for sensitive browsing, Firefox with extensions for daily use, and a stock browser for sites that break with modifications.

items.why: Many fingerprinting attempts happen invisibly. Detection tools help you identify which sites are attempting to fingerprint your device.
items.howTo: Install Ghostery, Privacy Badger, or uBlock Origin with additional filter lists. Enable logging to see blocked fingerprinting attempts.

items.task: Rotate browser profiles and clear data
items.why: Even with protections, some fingerprint data accumulates over time. Fresh profiles prevent long-term tracking correlation.
items.howTo: Create new Firefox profiles monthly, or Use a privacy-focused browser's session isolation. Clear all browser data including local storage and IndexedDB.

items.why: VPNs hide your IP but don't prevent fingerprinting. Combining both provides comprehensive protection against tracking techniques.
items.howTo: Use a no-logs VPN service with your fingerprint protection setup. Ensure WebRTC is disabled to prevent IP leaks that could correlate with fingerprints.

pro_tips: Privacy-focused browsers provides comprehensive fingerprinting protection out-of-the-box, including canvas spoofing, WebGL blocking, and timezone masking without requiring manual configuration.
Don't make your browser too unique - overly aggressive fingerprint protection can actually make you more identifiable. Aim to blend in with common configurations.
Test your fingerprint protection on multiple testing sites, as each site checks different fingerprinting vectors and may reveal weaknesses in your setup.
Mobile browsers are particularly vulnerable to fingerprinting due to sensor access and touch capabilities. Consider using privacy-focused mobile browsers for sensitive browsing.
Fingerprinting protection often breaks some websites. Keep a separate browser profile with standard settings for sites that require full functionality.
